chapter.title: Bathrooms
chapter.segment_label: Chapter 6 segment covering printed pages 170-187, from 'Ergonomics and Required Clearances' through the end of 'Lighting' and the chapter References list. Earlier pages of the chapter were not provided.

coverage_audit.notes: All 18 provided pages were rasterized and inspected visually in addition to the text layer. Figures 6-25 through 6-39 were opened as enlarged crops so that dimension lines, callout numbers and figure notes could be read directly rather than inferred; several values recorded here (for example the fixture centreline offsets in Figure 6-26a/b, the transfer-tub and roll-in-shower geometry in Figure 6-27, the knee and toe clearances in Figure 6-28a, and the 42 inch receptacle height in Figure 6-38) exist only in the drawings and not in the running text. The chapter References list on printed page 187 was recorded as an excluded source item. coverage_complete refers to the provided segment only; earlier pages of Chapter 6 were not supplied.

top_findings.why_useful: The bathroom equivalent of a work triangle: rules of thumb that order sink, toilet and bathing fixtures relative to the entry door, giving RemLab a placement sequence rather than only isolated clearances.
Standard toilet clear zone with both minimum and recommended width and depth, and with the bounding element generalized to 'fixture, wall or door' - directly usable as a clearance primitive.
IRC P2705 gives the code floor (381 mm centreline, 533 mm in front) beneath the more generous recommended values elsewhere in the chapter, so RemLab can distinguish hard constraints from preferences.
A rare explicit parametric relationship: a second sink increases room area by 35 percent, which supports program sizing rather than only conflict checking.
Shower door swing direction is conditional on stall size, an example of a genuine conditional rule that must not be flattened into a constant.
